title: Lesson 7: Event-Driven Integration: Platform Events + Change Data Capture
description: The Salesforce event bus, Platform Events vs. Change Data Capture: when to publish business intent vs. record state, how to consume on- and off-platform, and the hard truth about ordering, replay, and allocations.

questions.question: What distinguishes a Platform Event from Change Data Capture?
options: A Platform Event carries a designed payload for business intent; CDC carries record state.
A Platform Event only ever reports record deletions, while CDC reports only record creations.
A Platform Event needs no subscriber, while CDC requires a custom payload.
A Platform Event lives only in memory, while CDC is written to disk.
questions.explanation: Platform Events let you define a message for business intent, while CDC automatically publishes the changed record's fields, noise from bulk loads included.

questions.question: How should a consumer reconstruct the order of CDC changes from one save?
options: Sort every event by its ReplayId, which is contiguous and unique.
Trust commitNumber, which is a guaranteed and globally unique key for ordering events.
Assume the event bus delivers every change in strict global order.
Group by transactionKey, then order within the group by sequenceNumber.
questions.explanation: The bus does not guarantee strict order, so consumers group by transactionKey and use sequenceNumber within a transaction, treating commitNumber as diagnostic.

questions.question: Why must a subscriber persist and reuse its ReplayId?
options: To convert a Platform Event stream into a Change Data Capture stream.
To resume a stream after a disconnect and catch up on missed events.
To raise the daily delivery allocation available to the org.
To make replay IDs contiguous and simple to compute by hand.
questions.explanation: Replay IDs mark a position in the stream, so storing the last one lets a consumer reconnect and replay missed events within the retention window.
